title: Major AI-agent platform ships zero-trust controls as default-on by Q2 2027
body: By Q2 2027 at least one major AI-agent platform, agent-orchestration vendor, or agentic IDE will ship zero-trust controls as default-on in a named release, not as an opt-in flag. The qualifying posture shift is deny-by-default per-tenant flow- or object-level authorization (closing cross-tenant insecure-direct-object-reference gaps like the Langflow flaw, where get_flow_by_id_or_endpoint_name resolved a flow by UUID with no owner check) and/or default outbound-egress allowlisting with SSRF-hardened tool-call and web-request blocks (closing primitives like AutoGPT's SendWebRequestBlock, whose IPv4-mapped-IPv6 parsing gap re-opened the internal-IP filter). The forcing function is structural: this week alone produced a CVSS 9.9 cross-tenant IDOR in Langflow with first in-the-wild exploitation reported by Sysdig on June 25, and a CVSS 8.5 SSRF bypass in AutoGPT (CVE-2026-56663, fixed in 0.6.52, June 26). Both prove the orchestration and execution plane ships without zero-trust defaults, and a fetch-arbitrary-URL block is by construction an SSRF surface. What does NOT count: a blog post or best-practices doc, an opt-in toggle a customer must enable, a one-off CVE patch with no default-posture change, or a roadmap promise. The qualifying event is a default-on capability gate that authenticates and authorizes per tenant before a flow executes or an outbound request leaves the runner.

reasoning.because: Langflow's live-exploited CVSS 9.9 cross-tenant IDOR and AutoGPT's CVSS 8.5 SSRF bypass hit agents
reasoning.given: the agent orchestration layer ships without deny-by-default per-tenant authz or egress allowlisting
reasoning.so_that: a major agent platform, orchestration vendor, or agentic IDE ships zero-trust controls default-on in a named release
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; named release defaulting to per-tenant authz or egress allowlisting
reasoning.plain_language: Two agent tools got hacked through missing access checks this week, so a big agent platform will soon make strict per-tenant security on by default.

summary: Twin agent-platform CVEs this week (Langflow's live-exploited cross-tenant IDOR, AutoGPT's SSRF bypass) expose an orchestration layer with no zero-trust defaults. By Q2 2027 a major agent platform or agentic IDE ships deny-by-default per-tenant authz or egress allowlisting default-on in a release.
